title: Is ANSYS Free for Students? Ansys Student 2026 R1 Limits, Download and Install
summary: Yes: Ansys Student is free for verified students, Windows only, with 128K-node structural and 1M-cell CFD limits. What it includes, renewal and install steps.
body_markdown:
## Is ANSYS free for students?


**Yes.** Ansys Student is a free, official download of the Ansys Workbench bundle (Mechanical, Fluent, CFX, Discovery, SpaceClaim and more) for verified students. It runs only on 64-bit Windows 10/11, is for educational use only, caps problem size at 128K nodes/elements for structural and 1 million cells/nodes for fluids, and comes on a renewable 12-month licence.


Everything below was checked on Ansys's own student pages on **17 November 2026** . Ansys is now part of Synopsys, so the old ansys.com student links redirect to **ansys.synopsys.com** . The newest student build offered on that date is **2026 R1** ; the 2025 R2 build is still listed too.


## What do you get in the free Ansys Student bundle?


The main download is the **Workbench-based bundle** . Per the[Ansys Student page](https://ansys.synopsys.com/academic/students/ansys-student) it includes:


Area Products in the free bundle


Structural FEA Ansys Mechanical, Mechanical APDL, Autodyn, Motion (2026 R1 only)


CFD Fluent and CFX, TurboGrid, Polyflow, Chemkin-Pro


Geometry Discovery, SpaceClaim, DesignModeler


Optimisation and post optiSLang, EnSight


Particles and optics Rocky (DEM/SPH), SPEOS, Zemax OpticStudio


Three products are **separate free downloads** , each with its own limits: **Electronics Desktop Student** (HFSS, Maxwell, Q3D, Icepak, Twin Builder, Circuit), **LS-DYNA Student** (explicit dynamics, crash) and Scade One.


## What are the Ansys Student limits?


These are the problem-size caps Ansys publishes for the student products:


Sponsored


175+ hours of industry projects & 12 IIT faculty sessions


Master CATIA, NX, LS-DYNA, HyperMesh and more


View Full Curriculum


Product Limit (as of 17 Nov 2026)


Structural physics (Mechanical, APDL) **128K nodes/elements**


Fluid physics (Fluent, CFX) **1 million cells/nodes**


Parallel solving (HPC) **4 CPU cores** , plus 40 GPU SMs on Fluent


Rocky 32K DEM particles, 128K SPH particles


SPEOS up to 50 bodies and 300 faces


HFSS / Maxwell / Q3D 64,000 3D volume elements, 8,000 3D surface elements, 2,000 2D triangles


Icepak 512K elements


LS-DYNA Student 128K nodes/elements


**What fits in 128K?** Enough for every coursework problem: a bracket, a shaft with a fillet, a plate with a hole, a beam or truss model, a modal study of a small part. It runs out on full assemblies and very fine meshes. The usual workarounds are the ones industry uses anyway: model a half or a quarter when the geometry and loads are symmetric (a quarter-symmetry model needs roughly a quarter of the nodes), use beam and shell elements for thin parts instead of solid elements, and refine the mesh only where stresses change fast.


For CFD, **1 million cells** covers 2D studies, pipe and duct flow, flow over a cylinder or airfoil, and coarse 3D external aerodynamics. A detailed 3D car body with a resolved boundary layer will not fit.


## Who can download Ansys Student?


Ansys now checks who you are. The student page says the bundle is offered "for verified students and educators", and the Electronics page puts it plainly: "Ansys free student downloads are NO longer openly available." Verification runs through **SheerID** using your college details and is valid for one year. Indian students verify the same way as everyone else; the India (en-in) pages carry the same terms, with no India-only offer.


## What are the Ansys Student system requirements?


Requirement Main Workbench bundle


Operating system **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit** only (no macOS, no Linux build for students)


RAM 4 GB minimum (8 GB for Discovery)


Disk 50 GB free on a physical C: drive


Graphics OpenGL professional card; Discovery needs an NVIDIA GPU with 4 GB+ video memory (8 GB preferred)


In practice, 4 GB of RAM only opens the software. **16 GB** is the comfortable minimum for meshing and solving models near the 128K limit. Electronics Desktop Student asks for 8 GB RAM and 17 GB of disk; LS-DYNA Student asks for 4 GB RAM and 25 GB of disk. Mac users need a Windows PC: Ansys lists no macOS build. Our[laptop guide for engineering students](https://resources.skill-lync.com/articles/best-laptop-for-engineering-students-india/) covers which hardware runs Ansys well and what happens on a Mac.
